notes: THE QUESTION ASKED — ARE THE TWO ISEMCO PAGES THE SAME REGISTERED DEGREE? Answer, stated plainly: **by the page's own diploma statement they are NOT the same registered degree, but on the weight of all the other evidence on the page they are — this URL is a stale, internally contradictory page that has been repointed.** The full reasoning, on the three tests I was asked to apply: (1) RUCT CODES — these differ and this is the decisive test. batch-03.jsonl's record (sourced from ISEMCO slug .../master-en-direccion-y-produccion-de-eventos-comunicacion-corporativa-y-protocolo/) is RUCT 4312968, the UCJC title, «Publicado en B.O.E. (TITULACIÓN RENOVADA)». The title in THIS page's H1 and diplomas bullet is a genuinely different registered title, RUCT 4316273, «Máster Universitario en Dirección, Organización y Producción de Eventos Corporativos e Institucionales por la Universidad Rey Juan Carlos», which the register shows as «TITULACIÓN A EXTINGUIR» with extinction opened by the Comunidad de Madrid on 14/09/2023. Neither page prints a «Código RUCT» itself; I resolved both codes from output/ruct-backbone.jsonl and confirmed each against its own RUCT detail page. (2) ECTS — this test does NOT discriminate, and that is worth recording: both titles are 60 ECTS and both have the identical internal breakdown 48 obligatorias + 0 optativas + 6 prácticas externas + 6 TFM. Anyone using ECTS alone would wrongly conclude they are one degree. (3) AWARDING UNIVERSITY — differs: Universidad Camilo José Cela (private, Madrid) versus Universidad Rey Juan Carlos (public, Madrid), and the two titles are registered to entirely different teaching centres — UCJC's Facultad de Comunicación y Diseño (28051748) versus «Centro de Educación Superior CEDEU» (28053897), a URJC-attached private centre. ISEMCO is not the registered centre for either. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED TO THIS PAGE — the evidence is unambiguous and it is a document-archaeology finding, not a guess. The slug itself (master-universitario-organizacion-eventos) matches the URJC title's wording, not UCJC's; the page still serves a legacy PDF named **«Dossier-Master-oficial-CEDEU-2020.pdf»** — CEDEU being precisely the centre RUCT records for URJC 4316273 — alongside a 2022-vintage «solicitud_master_oficial-2022-2023.pdf»; and the H1 and the diplomas bullet still name the URJC title. Everything else on the page has been overwritten with UCJC content: the «Titulación a través de» caption sits directly above a UCJC logo file uploaded in 2022, the awarding sentence names UCJC and links ucjc.edu, the admission block links UCJC's own postgraduate application PDF on ucjc.edu, the «PORTAL ACADÉMICO» and «BECAS» sections are UCJC's, and the QS Stars block is about UCJC. The site's own navigation reinforces this: under «Másteres oficiales» it lists only two titles — the UCJC one and a Universidad del Atlántico Medio one (RUCT 4317071) — and this page's own H1 is NOT among them. So: this is the URJC/CEDEU master's old page, recycled to sell the UCJC master after the URJC title went into extinction, with the H1 and one bullet never updated. I have therefore recorded 4312968 as the operative code and 4316273 as the superseded one, exactly as the a-extinguir trap is handled elsewhere in this dataset. WHAT THIS RECORD DUPLICATES: the UCJC/ISEMCO record already in output/spring/enrich/batch-03.jsonl, whose institution field reads «UCJC — Universidad Camilo José Cela (programme delivered with ISEMCO...)» and which carries RUCT 4312968. Its fee, rate-year and extra-fee figures are reused here with attribution rather than re-derived, because ucjc.edu would not serve me today (202 shell x3, then 403). The campus, modality, places, February-cohort, EUR 40 admission fee, language and admission-documentation facts in THIS record are read directly off the page at the URL above and are not carried over. ACTION REQUIRED BEFORE THIS PROGRAMME CAN BE RANKED: a human must ask ISEMCO in writing which of the two degrees a February-2027 enrolee actually receives. The page as it stands promises a degree (URJC 4316273) that the national register says has been winding down since 14/09/2023, while describing a different one (UCJC 4312968) that is live. That is not a cosmetic error — it is the difference between a currently accredited award and one that may no longer admit students. ONE OBSERVATION ON THE SIBLING RECORD, offered because it affects how much weight to put on what I reused: batch-03 drew its admission-dossier and apostille details from ISEMCO's «master-en-direccion-y-produccion-de-eventos-comunicacion-corporativa-y-protocolo» page, which ISEMCO's own navigation files under «OTROS MÁSTERES Y ESPECIALISTAS» rather than under «Másteres oficiales» — i.e. that page markets a título propio. The identical EUR 40 / apostille wording appears on THIS page too, in the context of the official master, so the substance holds; but it is a reminder that on this site official and non-official products share boilerplate and cannot be told apart by page furniture. CANDIDATE FIT: path code S (Events, Festival & Live Entertainment Management). The subject matter has real overlap with the candidate's music-industry side — the practicum list on this page names Festival Rototom, Festival A Summer Story, DGTL Madrid, DreamBeach, Brunch in the Park, Universal Music Festival, RLM artist management and Premios Goya/Forqué/Platino, which is a genuinely strong live-events network. Against that: it is Spanish-only, it is a private-university fee with no public-fee route, and it has nothing to do with the candidate's software-engineering background, so no credit recognition against the 300 ECTS is plausible here. ACCESS FOR A NON-EEA DEGREE, verbatim from this page: applicants entering a Máster Universitario with a foreign qualification must supply a «Certificado o carta de la Universidad de origen, acreditando que con su titulación se puede acceder a estudios de Postgrado y/o Maestrías»; non-EU applicants must present the degree certificate and academic transcript bearing the Hague apostille (EU applicants need only originals or a notarised copy). Full dossier: solicitud de admisión, DNI/pasaporte, certificado académico de notas, título or proof of fee payment, CV, carta de motivación, and the EUR 40 transfer receipt. No homologación of the prior degree is demanded for admission. COMPLEMENTOS FORMATIVOS: RUCT publishes no «Nº Créditos Complementos Formativos» row for 4312968 — that is NOT PUBLISHED IN RUCT, which is not the same as 0 — and none for 4316273 either; neither this page nor the register states an applicant-level rule.

europe_recognition: EHEA level 7 (Bologna) — academic recognition across the EHEA, on BRIEF case (a). Legal basis, all read off the RUCT detail page for 3500484: official Spanish Máster Universitario, «Nivel MECES: 3» = EQF/EHEA level 7, second cycle, constituted under RD 822/2021, Acuerdo del Consejo de Ministros published in the BOE on 01/10/2025, institutional accreditation renewed 21/10/2024. It carries a Diploma Supplement as of right — UPC charges 218,15 € to issue the official degree certificate with the European Diploma Supplement — and grants access to doctoral study. THE TWO LIMITS THAT MATTER HERE, and the first of them bites unusually hard on this particular degree. (i) EHEA academic recognition is NOT professional recognition, and this master is precisely a case where the difference is substantive rather than theoretical: RUCT records «Habilita para profesión regulada: Sí — Ingeniero Industrial», so what the degree confers in Spain is the legal attribution to practise a REGULATED profession. Those attributions are a Spanish national entitlement. Carrying them into another EU/EEA state is not part of EHEA academic recognition at all — it runs through Directive 2005/36/EC and the receiving state's own competent-authority procedure, which may impose an aptitude test or adaptation period. So a graduate may have their qualification academically recognised in, say, France or Germany while still not being authorised to sign off as an engineer there. Anyone valuing this degree for its habilitante status must understand that the habilitación is the part that travels LEAST well. (ii) Academic recognition abroad still requires the receiving country's own procedure — the EHEA and the Lisbon Recognition Convention make that routine, not automatic. NOTE ON THE STALE LINK: the page's «Official degree — Recorded in the Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities» link resolves to RUCT 4314000, which has been in extinction since 01/08/2025. That does not weaken the recognition analysis — 4314000 is itself MECES 3 and EQF 7, and anyone who already holds it holds a fully recognised degree — but a 2027 entrant must be enrolled on 3500484, and the recognition evidence to quote is 3500484's, not the link the page gives you.
tuition_eu_eur: EUR 2,122 (2026-27 rates) — printed on the page itself, in both the English and the Catalan original («2.122 € (5.400 € per a no residents a la UE)»), as the approximate master's fee EXCLUDING other costs («no inclou taxes acadèmiques de caràcter no docent ni expedició del títol»). UPC's own fees page additionally gives an ALL-IN estimate that «inclou les principals taxes» for a 120-credit habilitant master: **EUR 2,800** for EU students. Both figures are UPC's own; 2,122 is tuition alone and 2,800 is tuition plus the main administrative fees.
tuition_non_eu_eur: EUR 5,400 (2026-27 rates) — tuition alone, printed on the page itself. UPC's all-in estimate including the main fees for a 120-credit habilitant master is **EUR 6,100** for «estudiants no comunitaris (no resident Unió Europea)». This is the figure that matters for this candidate: 45.00 €/credit against the EU/resident 17.69 €/credit is a **2.54x multiplier**, and it is charged as a single differentiated total price, not as a surcharge added to the resident rate. Decret 96/2026 art. 1.5 is explicit that a Spanish long-stay study authorisation «no equival a la condició de residents», so a Tunisian citizen cannot escape it by enrolling and living in Catalonia. RESIT RISK, which nobody should overlook on a 120-ECTS habilitante master: UPC's per-credit table charges non-EU non-resident students **60 €/credit on a 2nd enrolment, 100 € on a 3rd and 128 € on a 4th** — against 21,85 / 47,84 / 65,55 € for a resident on a habilitant master. Failing and repeating credits is therefore roughly 2.5x more expensive for this candidate than for a local, on a demanding two-year technical degree taught in a language they do not yet speak.

notes: THE DECISIVE QUESTION — SAME TITLE AT A SECOND CENTRE, OR A SEPARATE TITLE? Answer: **the SAME registered title, delivered at a second centre.** This is settled directly from the register and is not an inference. The RUCT detail page for 3500484 («Máster Universitario en Ingeniería Industrial por la Universidad Politécnica de Catalunya») carries a «Centros en los que se imparte» block reading «2 registros encontrados, mostrando todos los registros», and the two rows are: 08072671 «Escuela Superior de Ingenierías Industrial, Aeroespacial y Audiovisual de Terrassa» and 08032853 «Escuela Técnica Superior de Ingeniería Industrial de Barcelona». So ESEIAAT Terrassa is explicitly listed as a teaching centre of the very title that output/spring/enrich/batch-07.jsonl already records for ETSEIB Barcelona. One RUCT code, one degree, two schools. The superseded code 4314000 has the identical two-centre structure, so this has been a two-centre title throughout its life. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE MERGE — DO NOT DEDUPLICATE THESE TWO RECORDS. They share a RUCT code but they are different products to an applicant: different city (Terrassa vs Barcelona), different intake sizes (100+80 here), different speciality menus, and a materially different language statement. ESEIAAT offers 8 specialisations — Biomedical Engineering, Construction and Structures, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Organization, Mechanical Engineering, Paper and Graphic Technology, Textile Design and Technology, Thermal Energy — of which Paper and Graphic Technology and Textile Design and Technology are Terrassa-only, reflecting the school's historic textile-engineering identity. The register lists 14 especialidades for the title as a whole (including Automática y Robótica, Ingeniería Nuclear, Electrónica, Ambientalización de Procesos, Energía and Tecnologías de la Información para la Industria), i.e. the ETSEIB menu is different again. A merge that collapses these on RUCT code alone would lose the campus, which is one of the fields this dataset exists to record. THE A-EXTINGUIR TRAP, CONFIRMED PRESENT ON THIS PAGE. The Terrassa page's «Official degree / Recorded in the Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities» link points at CodigoEstudio=**4314000**. That code's RUCT detail page shows «Fecha inicio extinción … 01/08/2025» recorded by the Comunitat Autònoma de Catalunya, is constituted under the older «Máster – RD 1393/2007 (1)», and has a different internal credit split (65 obligatorios + 43 optativos + 12 TFM = 120). The LIVE title is 3500484, under RD 822/2021, with 60 obligatorios + 45 optativos + 0 prácticas + 15 TFM = 120, authorised by the Generalitat on exactly 01/08/2025 — the same day 4314000's extinction opened. Recorded 3500484 as the live code and 4314000 as the superseded one. This is the identical stale link the ETSEIB page carries, so it is a UPC site-wide problem, not a Terrassa-specific one. FEE ARITHMETIC, shown as the brief requires. Industrial Engineering is named in Decret 96/2026 annex 2 among the masters qualifying for a regulated profession, so it is HABILITANT and takes the lower resident credit price. I read UPC's own 2026-27 per-credit table directly today and it prints: «Màster universitari habilitant 17,69 €», «Màster universitari no habilitant 19,37 €», «Màster universitari habilitant i no habilitant (no residents, no UE) 45 €» (first enrolment). Therefore 17,69 x 120 = 2.122,80 → the 2.122 € the page prints, and 45,00 x 120 = 5.400,00 → the 5.400 € the page prints. Both check out exactly, which independently confirms the habilitant classification. Note that the non-EU 45 € is a single differentiated TOTAL price, not an increment on 17,69 €. CONFLICT — UPC'S OWN FAQ IS STALE AND MUST NOT BE USED. The UPC master's FAQ still states the non-EU non-resident per-credit price is **102,52 €**. That contradicts UPC's own 2026-27 price table (45 €), contradicts Decret 96/2026, and contradicts the 5.400 € total printed on this very programme page; 102,52 x 120 would give 12.302 €, more than double the page's own figure. Logged as a CONFLICT and NOT used. The 45 € figure is the one consistent with every published total. THE 300-ECTS QUESTION. RUCT publishes no «Nº Créditos Complementos Formativos» row for 3500484 — that is NOT PUBLISHED IN RUCT, which is not the same as 0. The programme page does state an applicant-level rule, and it is a real one: the Catalan «Requisits específics» list admits graduates of the grau en Enginyeria en Tecnologies Industrials, holders of Enginyeria Industrial, and graduates of degrees giving access to the regulated profession of enginyer/a tècnic/a industrial, and then adds «Enginyeries Tècniques: amb complements de formació» — bridging credits for technical-engineering entrants. CANDIDATE FIT — THIS IS A POOR MATCH AND THE RECORD SHOULD SAY SO PLAINLY. The candidate holds a 300-ECTS SOFTWARE engineering degree from SMU MedTech Tunisia. Software engineering does not appear in the access list, which is built entirely around industrial-technologies and technical-industrial engineering pathways feeding a Spanish regulated profession. The value of this degree is overwhelmingly the «Ingeniero Industrial» habilitación, which is a Spanish professional entitlement of limited portability and of no obvious use to this candidate's stated fields (audio technology, MIR, AI/ML, data science, cloud, events, music industry). Add the Catalan/Spanish-only teaching and there is no English route at all. Where credits ARE recognised the cost drops sharply — Decret 96/2026 art. 6.1 charges recognised/validated credits at 20% of the normal price, i.e. 9,00 €/credit for a non-EU student rather than 45,00 € — so any advanced standing granted against the 300 ECTS is worth roughly five times its face value in fee terms. But that is a consolation on a degree the candidate should probably not be applying to. FOREIGN DOCUMENTS: the page states that all documents issued in non-EU countries «must be legalised and bear the corresponding apostille» / «legalitzats per via diplomàtica o amb la postil·la corresponent». PRE-ENROLMENT was closed at the date of access with no 2027 window published; the page directs applicants to the «Request information» form for upcoming periods.
